title: Issue #1791: Aggregate Row Layout
body:
This is a very preliminary PR, but I wanted to submit it so we could look at the approach. It also fixes an issue where we were not passing in the binding data for the aggregate function calls, so it seemed worth a push. Biding data is not used often, but `QUANTILE` and some other multi-argument aggregates do use it.

Basically, I have factored out column locations into a separate `RowLayout` object that manages the row storage for validity masks, data (key or group) columns and aggregate states. The calls to aggregate methods in the two hash tables were then wrapped in a new `RowOperations` namespace/struct. Some code tidying and simplification also came out of the work.

The longer term plan is to:
* Refactor the scatter and gather operations for populating and reading data so they can be shared 
* Extend the row layout management to the join hash table (this will enable `GroupJoin` support)
* Add in support for nested types (this will enable hashing and joining on `STRUCT`, `LIST` and `MAP`(?!) types simultaneously
* Add disk spooling to support out-of-memory operation
* Merge it with the sorting representations (this will hopefully be relatively straightforward if the previous two items are done intelligently.)
